documents.title: Investing in Gold – Market Timing or Buy-and-Hold?
documents.research_question: Can gold be actively timed vs. buy-and-hold using seasonal, technical, and fundamental signals?
documents.methodology: 4000+ strategies tested; Hansen SPA test for multiple-testing control; stepwise SPA extensions; transaction costs included
documents.key_findings: Some strategies show gains but NOT robust to data-snooping (SPA p>0.05); gains period-specific; conclusion: gold market efficient
documents.statistical_significance: SPA test controls family-wise error rate; no strategy survives correction
documents.relevance_reason: Monthly frequency, no intraday mechanisms, negative result after multiple testing correction

documents.title: Cross-Asset Price-Based Regimes for Gold
documents.research_question: Does joint momentum of gold + long-duration Treasuries identify macro regimes that improve gold timing?
documents.methodology: Dual-momentum regime classifier (Gold mom x Treasury mom); 4 regimes; long-only timing; standardized z-score signals; OOS evaluation
documents.key_findings: Dual-momentum improves Sharpe (0.42->0.51) and reduces max DD (-60%->-37%); falling real rate regime (Gold+/Treasury+) best; positive gold momentum alone predictive; Treasury momentum refines regime
documents.transaction_costs: Not explicitly modelled; cash uses Fed Funds rate
documents.statistical_significance: Descriptive performance comparison; no formal tests
documents.relevance_reason: Regime concept (real rates, risk appetite) transfers to intraday; cross-asset momentum could be proxied via H1/D1 correlations

documents.title: Ultra-high-frequency pairs trading in gold ETFs
documents.research_question: Can pairs trading of gold ETFs generate excess returns at ultra-high frequency?
documents.methodology: Cointegration-based pairs selection; formation/trading periods; full vs partial convergence exit (40% optimal); bid-ask + commission costs
documents.key_findings: Full convergence: 2.1% p.a. after costs; Partial convergence (40%): 3.38% p.a. after costs; consistent across sub-samples; returns exceed risk compensation -> UHF inefficiency
documents.statistical_significance: t-tests on returns; robustness across sub-samples
documents.relevance_reason: UHF mechanism (ms arbitrage across ETFs) does not transfer to M5 single-instrument trading; no pairs on Exness XAUUSDm

documents.title: Cryptocurrency Volume-Weighted Time Series Momentum
documents.research_question: Does volume-weighting improve TSMOM in crypto?
documents.methodology: Volume-weighted Winner-Minus-Loser (VW-WML) portfolio; weight by daily volume (not market cap); compare VW/IV/EW/CW; wash trading controls; 3-factor model
documents.key_findings: VW-WML: 0.94%/day, Sharpe 2.17; outperforms EW/CW/IV; not explained by market/size/momentum factors; robust to wash-trading controls
documents.statistical_significance: t-stats on portfolio returns; factor model alphas
documents.relevance_reason: Asset class mismatch (crypto vs gold); volume-weighting concept could transfer (tick volume on M5) but microstructure differs

documents.title: Are Simple Technical Trading Rules Profitable in Bitcoin Markets?
documents.research_question: Can simple technical rules beat buy-and-hold in BTC after costs and data-mining correction?
documents.methodology: 75,360 simple rules (6 classes x frequencies); FDR multiple testing control; select best after costs; portfolio formation; OOS evaluation
documents.key_findings: Some rules outperform risk-return wise OOS; after FDR correction significance diminishes; intraday (10-min) better than daily; costs critical; long-only variants better
documents.transaction_costs: Average daily bid-ask spread + minimum fee (Bitstamp)
limitations: FDR conservative but still multiple testing concern
documents.relevance_reason: Methodology (FDR, OOS, cost-aware) directly transferable; 10-min frequency closer to M5; but asset class mismatch, BTC 24/7 vs gold sessions

documents.title: Bitcoin Time-of-Day, Day-of-Week and Month-of-Year Effects in Returns and Trading Volume
documents.research_question: Do time-of-day, day-of-week, month-of-year anomalies exist in Bitcoin?
documents.methodology: Heatmaps of returns/volume by hour/day/month; statistical tests; cross-exchange comparison; session alignment with US equity hours
documents.key_findings: Lower weekend volume; higher Monday returns (currency-like); increased activity during US equity hours; USD exchanges stronger patterns; NO consistent/persistent patterns; conclusion: weak-form efficient
documents.relevance_reason: Session-based analysis directly relevant; gold has clear Asian/European/US sessions; time-of-day effects may exist; methodology directly applicable

documents.title: Dual Momentum Allocation Between Physical Gold and Bitcoin (Digital Gold)
documents.research_question: Can dual-momentum allocation between gold and Bitcoin improve risk-adjusted returns?
documents.methodology: Dual momentum (absolute + relative); weekly rebalancing; GLD NYSE days; BTC Bitfinex hourly aligned to GLD close; volatility targeting implied
documents.key_findings: BTC: 46.66% CAGR, 64% vol, 0.73 Sharpe, -77% DD; GLD: 18.8% CAGR, 17% vol, 1.10 Sharpe, -21% DD; 50/50: 38.65% CAGR, 34% vol, 1.12 Sharpe, -51% DD; dual momentum aims to rotate
documents.relevance_reason: Dual momentum concept transfers; but weekly frequency, ETF vehicles only, Bitcoin component irrelevant per programme constraints

documents.title: Revisiting Trend-following and Mean-reversion Strategies in Bitcoin
documents.research_question: Do MAX (trend-following) and MIN (mean-reversion) strategies work on Bitcoin?
documents.methodology: MAX: buy at x-day max (trend continuation); MIN: buy at x-day min (mean reversion); lookbacks 10/20/30/40/50 days; in-sample vs extended
documents.key_findings: Both strategies 'alive and effective, especially 10-day'; MAX stronger than MIN (higher returns, lower DD); both 'efficient for trading'
documents.relevance_reason: Asset mismatch; daily frequency; no cost model; MAX/MIN similar to Assignment 14 Donchian which was REJECTED

documents.title: How To Profitably Trade Bitcoin's Overnight Sessions
documents.research_question: Does overnight anomaly exist in Bitcoin; can it be exploited?
documents.methodology: Decompose daily vs overnight sessions; analyze day-of-week/weekend effects; build seasonal strategy; hypothesis: ETF flows tied to TradFi hours
documents.key_findings: Incomplete excerpt - full results not visible
documents.relevance_reason: Session decomposition directly relevant; gold has clear overnight (Asian) vs daytime (Europe/US) structure; Wei 2026 shows Asian session dominates gold returns

documents.title: Seasonality, Trend-following, and Mean reversion in Bitcoin
documents.research_question: Do seasonality, trend-following, and mean-reversion effects exist in Bitcoin?
documents.methodology: Seasonality: NYSE open/close effects, intraday/overnight; 2-hour holding strategy; MAX/MIN trend/mean-reversion; lookbacks 10-50 days; hourly data
documents.key_findings: 2-hour holding strategy positive; BTC trends at max, reverts at min; both trend-following and mean-reversion coexist (horizon-dependent); short-term reversal vs longer momentum
documents.relevance_reason: Hourly frequency, session-based seasonality directly relevant; NYSE open/close maps to London/NY session opens for gold; 2-hour holding maps to M5 session-window strategies

documents.title: Intraday Return Predictability in the Cryptocurrency Markets: Momentum, Reversal, or Both
documents.research_question: Is there intraday momentum and/or reversal in crypto?
documents.methodology: High-frequency data; first 30-min return predicts last 30-min return; condition on jumps, FOMC, liquidity, COVID; economic value vs benchmarks; late-informed investor theory
documents.key_findings: BOTH intraday momentum AND reversal exist; patterns change with jumps/FOMC/liquidity/COVID; momentum: first 30-min predicts last 30-min positively; reversal: unique to crypto (overreaction); timing strategy beats benchmarks; also in ETH/LTC/XRP
documents.statistical_significance: Regression-based predictability tests; economic value metrics
limitations: Late-informed mechanism may not transfer to gold
documents.relevance_reason: Intraday momentum/reversal at minute level relevant to M5; first/last half-hour maps to session open/close; but crypto 24/7 vs gold sessions; different participants

documents.title: Who Moves the Price? Trading-Session Return Decomposition and Cross-Session Momentum in Gold and Silver Markets
documents.timeframe: Hourly (3 UTC sessions: Asia 00-08, Europe 08-14:30, US 14:30-24)
documents.research_question: How are gold/silver returns distributed across sessions? Is there cross-session momentum?
documents.methodology: Decompose cumulative log returns by session (Lou/Polk/Skouras 2019); session returns chain to total; session momentum rule: long t+1 if session t > 0; cost 0.02% per position change; long-only and long/short
documents.key_findings: Asia: +77.2% gold, +61.7% silver (positive every year); Europe: +36.2%, +46.6%; US: -13.4%, -8.2% (highest vol, zero/negative drift); Session momentum autocorr: Gold +0.13, Silver +0.12 (Asia continuation); Before costs: momentum beats B&H; After 0.02%: only long-only survives (Gold Sharpe 1.68, ~half DD; Silver Sharpe 0.84, DD -53.6% -> -26.2%); US session momentum loses net
limitations: 0.02% cost may not reflect Exness spread+commission
documents.relevance_reason: Only paper studying XAU/USD spot directly with session decomposition; Asian session dominance (77% of returns) is structural; cross-session momentum (+0.13 autocorr) testable at M5/H1; cost model provides benchmark; strongest evidence for gold-specific intraday strategy

documents.title: Catching Crypto Trends: A Tactical Approach for Bitcoin and Altcoins
documents.research_question: Does ensemble Donchian trend-following work across crypto universe?
documents.methodology: Ensemble of Donchian channels (multiple lookbacks) -> single signal; volatility-based position sizing; rotational portfolio top 20 coins; cost mitigation technique; on-chain vs off-chain execution
documents.key_findings: Net-of-fees Sharpe > 1.5; annualized alpha 10.8% vs Bitcoin; cost mitigation effective; low correlation with traditional trend-following
limitations: Rotational portfolio not feasible on single-instrument XAUUSDm
documents.relevance_reason: Asset mismatch; daily; rotational not applicable; but ensemble Donchian + vol sizing + cost mitigation are methodological transfers; Assignment 14 already tested Donchian on XAUUSDm and REJECTED

documents.title: Research-to-Trade Process (Summary)
documents.research_question: Institutional workflow for turning research into automated validated trading strategies
documents.methodology: Idea -> Encode Rules -> Backtest -> Validate (MC, IS/OOS) -> Live Automated -> Monitor -> Iterate; Monte Carlo reshuffle & resample; 10k-20k runs; risk heuristics
documents.key_findings: 90-95% ideas from academic/industry research (SSRN); extract finding + 'why', don't copy; translate to testable rules; simple strategies often outperform; run multiple uncorrelated strategies; automate monitoring/risk
documents.statistical_significance: MC distribution analysis; red-flag thresholds after N trades
documents.relevance_reason: Operational playbook; defines validation standards (10k-20k MC runs, reshuffle+resample, IS/OOS, risk heuristics), rule components, translation process; must be followed rigorously

key_contradictions.description: Paper 1 (Baur et al.): No robust timing at monthly frequency after data-snooping correction
key_contradictions.vs: Paper 2 (Vojtko/Dujava): Dual-momentum regime improves gold timing at monthly frequency
key_contradictions.vs2: Paper 12 (Wei): Strong session-based predictability at hourly frequency
key_contradictions.resolution: Frequency matters. Monthly (1,2) != Hourly/Intraday (6,9,10,11,12). Session structure (12) distinct from trend-following (2,8,10,14). Assignment 14 tested trend-following + regime filter, not session momentum. Paper 12's session momentum is a different, untested hypothesis on XAUUSDm.

key_contradictions.vs: Assignment 14: H1-regime-filtered M5 Donchian on XAUUSDm REJECTED (IS: -99%, OOS: -20%)
key_contradictions.resolution: Asset class matters (BTC vs Gold). Frequency matters (Daily vs M5). Regime filter design matters. Donchian breakout itself not inherently profitable on XAUUSDm M5.

next_phase_mechanisms: Session return decomposition & cross-session momentum (Paper 12 - strongest)
Real-rate regime proxy at intraday (Paper 2 concept -> H1/D1)
